description: Returns how to submit one train, flight or TfL compensation claim on the company’s own form. Takes the claim type and the train operator or airline, with the journey date, ticket type, where it was booked and the airports as optional extras. Returns the eligibility rules for that company and claim type, the official claim page (marked unverified where Untap could not confirm it), numbered submission steps, each form field with where to find its value, the evidence to attach, the deadline (as a date when the journey date is given), any company rule on who may submit, what to expect after submitting and when to chase, the escalation route (operator to the Rail Ombudsman; airline to its dispute scheme, the CAA or a national enforcement body; TfL to London TravelWatch) and the sources with the dates they were checked. Covers every train operator in Untap’s Delay Repay engine, TfL and the airlines UK travellers fly most. Facts Untap has not verified come back marked as unknown rather than estimated. No sign-in needed. Journey details are not saved to an account; limited usage metadata is recorded.

arrival_airport.description: Three-letter arrival airport code, such as "LHR".

booked_via.description: Where the ticket was bought: from the operator or airline itself, from a ticket retailer such as Trainline, through a travel agent, or as part of a package holiday.

claim_type.description: What the claim is for: a late or cancelled train, a delayed or cancelled flight, denied boarding, a TfL incomplete journey or another TfL overcharge.

company.description: The train operator or airline, by name or code as people say it: "Southern", "LNER", "easyJet", "BA", "U2". Not needed for TfL.

departure_airport.description: Three-letter departure airport code, such as "CDG". Decides whether UK261 or EU261 applies, and with the arrival airport, the distance band.

journey_date.description: Date of travel, YYYY-MM-DD. With it, the result gives the last day to claim as a date.

ticket_type.description: Ticket type as printed, such as "Anytime Return", "Advance Single" or "Season". Decides the rail return-ticket rule.

name: get_claim_instructions
title: How to submit a train, flight or TfL claim
